stem: In the 6 to 11-year-old age group, 'persistent' asthma is defined by which of the following symptom patterns?

options.text: Waking overnight due to asthma symptoms more than twice per month.
Having symptoms that occur less than once every six weeks.
Experiencing one mild flare-up per year requiring only salbutamol.
Daytime symptoms occurring exactly once per month.

explanation: This frequency of nocturnal symptoms is a key indicator of persistent asthma requiring preventer therapy in this age group.
rationale: Look for a frequency of nighttime disturbances that indicates the disease is not adequately controlled.

optionExplanations.A: This frequency of nocturnal symptoms is a key indicator of persistent asthma requiring preventer therapy in this age group.
optionExplanations.B: This pattern is classified as 'infrequent intermittent' asthma.
optionExplanations.C: Occasional mild flares without interval symptoms do not meet the criteria for persistent asthma.
optionExplanations.D: Persistent asthma requires daytime symptoms more than once per week according to the source.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: Waking overnight due to asthma symptoms more than twice per month.
